title: Dirty pool
scenario: Committee Secretary: “Our caretaking agreement says the pool must be cleaned, skimmed and vacuumed weekly. The caretaker's log shows a clean on Thursday 1 October. The pool was filthy all weekend, so on Monday 5 October I told the manager to instruct daily cleaning from tomorrow. There's no variation or committee resolution changing the duty.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the secretary about the pool complaint?”

title: The non-resident manager
scenario: Lot Owner: “Our caretaker's agreement is titled Resident Unit Manager Agreement. Clause 6 requires him on site from 8 am to 5 pm, Monday to Friday, and he's there every weekday. But he lives in Carindale. I've only read the title page and clause 6, and I want him removed for not being resident.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the demand to remove the caretaker?”

title: Season change
scenario: Chairperson: “Our caretaker must mow fortnightly from October to March and monthly from April to September. The log shows the last mow on 14 September. It's now 2 October, 18 days later, and the grass is long. I've sent photos to the committee and called it a clear breach.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the alleged breach?”

title: The old caretaker's favours
scenario: Chairperson: “The management rights just transferred. For nine years the old caretaker washed the driveway weekly and collected owners' parcels. Neither task is in Schedule 2 and there's no deed of variation. The new caretaker has stopped both, and the committee wants a letter telling him to resume them immediately.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the proposed letter?”

title: Strings on the sale
scenario: Committee Member: “Our caretaker has applied to assign the agreement to a buyer, with settlement in five weeks. Window cleaning isn't a current duty. Four of our seven members want consent granted only if the buyer agrees to clean all external windows monthly at no extra charge.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the proposed condition?”

title: The top-up papers
scenario: Committee Member: “Our 74-lot scheme's draft EGM notice includes a motion to add a five-year extension to the caretaking agreement. The voting paper is an open ballot and allows proxies. There's no returning officer and no explanatory note. The notice is due to go out on Monday.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the draft notice?”

title: The early option
scenario: Chairperson: “Our caretaking agreement runs to 30 June 2028. Clause 4.2 lets the caretaker exercise the option for a further term at any time. On 5 October 2026, about 21 months early, he gave written notice exercising it. Several owners want the notice rejected as premature.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the option notice?”

title: As reasonably required
scenario: Committee Member: “The only cleaning duty in our agreement says clean common property as reasonably required. The lift interiors haven't been wiped in three weeks and we've had nine complaints. The committee wants a remedial action notice issued this week.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about taking action against the caretaker?”

title: Never done it before
scenario: Chairperson: “The buyer of our management rights has 12 years in hotel management but has never held management rights. Duties include pool chemicals, gardening, minor repairs and after-hours call-outs. The committee wants to refuse the assignment purely because of inexperience, without interviewing the buyer.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the proposed refusal?”

title: Notice today
scenario: Chairperson: “I've had enough of the state of the gardens. I want a remedial action notice issued to the caretaker today. The manager asked for the maintenance log on Monday and it's due Friday. Nobody has spoken to the caretaker or a solicitor.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about issuing the notice?”

title: The $380 drain
scenario: Treasurer: “Our agreement includes minor repairs up to $250 per item. Anything over that needs the committee's prior written approval. The caretaker cleared a blocked drain without asking and invoiced $380. One member wants to pay just the $130 above the limit.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the invoice?”

title: Tuesday afternoons
scenario: Lot Owner: “The caretaker must be on site 8 am to 5 pm weekdays. I've logged him absent from 2 to 4 pm on three Tuesdays running. He says he was buying parts for building repairs, but I don't believe him. I want a breach notice issued.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the alleged absences?”

title: The CPI bump
scenario: Treasurer: “The caretaker's remuneration is $96,000 a year, adjusted on 1 July by CPI. The CPI change was 3.4 per cent. Since July he's invoiced $8,400 a month, and we've already paid three of those invoices.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the caretaker's invoices?”

title: How's my levy worked out?
scenario: Lot Owner: “Our AGM approved an administrative fund budget of $233,000 and a sinking fund budget of $78,100. The scheme has 1,250 contribution schedule lot entitlements and my lot has 20. Nobody has explained how my levy was calculated.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about how the levy was set?”

title: The agent's figure
scenario: Lot Owner: “My lot has 20 contribution entitlements. The rate is $248.88 per entitlement, made up of $186.40 administrative and $62.48 sinking, paid in four quarterly instalments. My property manager says my quarterly bill should be $1,350.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the quarterly contribution?”

title: Ten cents
scenario: Accounts Officer: “The approved administrative fund rate is $186.40 per entitlement across 1,250 entitlements. The levy schedule in the system shows quarterly amounts of $46.60, $46.60, $46.60 and $46.50. Notices are due to be issued tomorrow.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the accounts officer about the levy schedule?”

title: Ten per cent?
scenario: Lot Owner: “I paid $4,620 in contributions last year and this year it's $4,977.60. That's a 10 per cent jump, and I want it raised at the next meeting as excessive.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the levy increase?”

title: Counting the cash
scenario: Treasurer: “Our gross quarterly contributions are $77,775. Owners who pay on time get a 10 per cent discount, and most of them do. I've built this quarter's cash flow forecast on receiving the full $77,775.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the cash flow forecast?”

title: The minus sign
scenario: Accounts Officer: “Lot 12 shows a balance of minus $612.30 on the aged-balance report. Its quarterly contribution is exactly $612.30 and the next instalment is due 1 January. The treasurer has asked whether it's an error.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the accounts officer about lot 12's balance?”

title: Christmas notices
scenario: Accounts Officer: “Our next contribution is due Friday 15 January 2027. Firm practice is to issue notices about six weeks ahead, and the regulation requires at least 30 days. Our office shuts from 21 December to 4 January.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the accounts officer about issuing the January notices?”

title: Lot 5's share
scenario: Lot Owner: “A general meeting approved a $90,000 special contribution for balcony repairs, levied on 900 contribution entitlements in two equal instalments. My lot has 14 entitlements. My notice says I owe $1,400 for the first instalment.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the instalment amount?”

title: Out of step
scenario: Chairperson: “We want our $90,000 special contribution due on 15 December and 15 March. Ordinary contributions fall due 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October. The balcony contractor needs its first progress payment in late January.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the instalment dates?”

title: Two days late
scenario: Lot Owner: “My gross quarterly contribution is $1,382.70, with a 10 per cent discount for paying on time. I paid $1,244.43 two days after the due date because of a bank delay. Now I've received a demand for $138.27, and I say I've paid in full.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the demand?”

title: Lot 18
scenario: Treasurer: “Lot 18 owes $3,840.55, now 95 days overdue. A reminder and a letter of demand have both been ignored. The committee meets on 20 October and I want to know what we should be deciding.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the committee's decision on lot 18?”

title: Put it in order
scenario: New Team Member: “I've written up our arrears process as: court claim, reminder notice, enforcement warrant, letter of demand, committee resolution to refer to a solicitor, judgment, internal follow-up call. I'm about to send it to a committee that asked how we chase debts.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the arrears process?”

title: The treasurer's Gmail
scenario: Treasurer: “I got two roof repair quotes, $18,400 and $21,950, by emailing contractors from my personal Gmail. An owner has asked for all correspondence about the roof quotes. They're my private emails and I don't intend to hand them over.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the records request?”
topic: What is a body corporate record

title: The CCTV request
scenario: Building Manager: “A car was scratched in the basement on 15 September. I saved two hours of CCTV to a USB stick; the system overwrites after 30 days. On 1 October the owner of lot 22, who isn't the car owner, emailed asking for a copy.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the building manager about handling the request?”

title: It'd be gone anyway
scenario: Chairperson: “Lot 22 has asked for the basement CCTV. I've told the building manager to delete the USB copy. The system would have overwritten it by now anyway, so we're just putting things back the way they'd be.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about deleting the footage?”

title: The keen buyer
scenario: Prospective Buyer: “I'm buying unit 9. I emailed asking for the last three years of committee minutes. I haven't paid any fee and the seller hasn't given me anything in writing, but settlement is in ten days and I need them now.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the buyer about the request?”

title: Everything
scenario: Lot Owner: “Your firm has managed our building for 14 years. I've emailed asking for all records concerning the building under my rights as an owner. I want everything.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the request?”

title: Where did the money go?
scenario: Lot Owner: “I want a summary of all body corporate spending from 2021 to 2025, broken down by category. I know audited statements exist for each year, but I want it in one table, and I say the manager has to prepare it.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the requested summary?”

title: Three piles
scenario: Lot Owner: “I've made a valid request for all committee emails about my by-law breach. I know there's legal advice in there, and someone called me a known troublemaker who lies. There are also emails just scheduling meetings. I want every email, unredacted, this week.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about releasing the emails?”
topic: Privilege and defamation risk in records

title: Paragraph 4
scenario: Lot Owner: “I asked for a two-page committee memo. The secretary says none of it can be released because paragraph 4 quotes the solicitor's advice. The other five paragraphs are about maintenance and the budget.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the memo?”

title: Just an internal worksheet
scenario: Accounts Officer: “Our team built an internal cash-flow worksheet. On 10 September the body corporate manager attached it to an email to the committee. An owner has asked for all financial documents given to the committee since July. I'm leaving the worksheet out because it's internal.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the accounts officer about the worksheet?”

title: The thin file
scenario: Team Member: “I'm replying to lot 4's dispute over a $1,200 water damage charge. The file holds his 3 September complaint, our 5 September reply and the plumber's invoice. I've heard the plumber sent photos, there was a VOC on 20 August, and the owner emailed again on 12 September. I'm ready to send my reply.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member before the reply goes out?”

title: The old scans
scenario: New Team Member: “Our scheme moves to a new management company on 1 November. I'm preparing the handover and leaving out the pre-2018 scanned files because they aren't text-searchable. There's also a USB of CCTV under a pending request that I wasn't sure about.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the records handover?”

title: Everything but the fee
scenario: Lot Owner: “On 28 September I emailed asking for the 2025 AGM minutes and the current insurance schedule. It's been two weeks and nothing's arrived. I haven't paid a fee because nobody told me there was one.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the request?”

title: The report that isn't
scenario: Lot Owner: “I've asked for the 2019 roof report and I'm told there isn't one. But the 2019 minutes say the roofer reported the membrane was in good condition. The chairperson has offered to write the report up from memory.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the roof report?”

title: Which rule book?
scenario: Residential Chairperson: “Our site has a residential scheme, a commercial scheme and a hotel lot. Each scheme has its own community management statement, and one building management statement covers all three. The shared car park boom gate needs a $2,900 repair, and the hotel says our CMS should decide who pays.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about sharing the repair cost?”

title: Copy and paste
scenario: Hotel Representative: “The new body corporate manager split our shared cleaning costs 60/40, the same as at his other site. He hadn't read our building management statement. We've already paid our share of $14,200 in recoveries this quarter.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the hotel representative about the recoveries?”

title: The roller door
scenario: Residential Treasurer: “We paid a $6,800 invoice for the shared driveway roller door. The building management statement splits driveway costs 45 per cent residential, 35 commercial and 20 hotel. The other parties haven't been asked to contribute.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about recovering the cost?”

title: Expired but still billing
scenario: Building Management Group Chair: “Your firm charges our group $1,150 a month for administration. The agreement expired on 31 December 2025 and was never renewed, yet we've been charged every month since.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the group chair about the fees?”

title: The wash-up
scenario: Hotel Representative: “The group estimated shared expenses at $120,000 and we paid our 20 per cent, $24,000. Actual costs came to $131,600. We've received an adjustment invoice, and we say the overrun should be split evenly between the three parties.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the hotel representative about the year-end adjustment?”

title: Two out of three
scenario: Residential Representative: “Our building management statement needs unanimous group approval to replace the shared fire panel for $62,000. Residential and commercial voted yes. The hotel voted no because it says the quote is too high. The fire contractor says the panel is near end of life.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the residential representative about the deadlock?”

title: The fire pump
scenario: Residential Treasurer: “A $2,450 fire pump service invoice was coded to our fire safety account and paid in full by us. The building management statement splits fire pump costs 45, 35 and 20 per cent.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the invoice?”

title: Two votes and fifty per cent
scenario: Commercial Representative: “We have the most floor area, so we should get two votes on the building management group. Hotel guests use the car park most, so the hotel should pay half of the $28,000 repair. The statement gives one vote each and splits car park costs 50, 30 and 20.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the commercial representative about both claims?”

title: By the bay
scenario: Hotel Representative: “Our building management statement shares car park costs by bays held. Residential has 120 bays, commercial 50 and we have 30. Resurfacing costs $40,000, and we've been billed a third.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the hotel representative about the resurfacing charge?”

title: Not their pool
scenario: Commercial Representative: “The pool is residential common property and isn't a shared facility under the building management statement. A $3,100 pool heater repair went through the group, and we were charged 35 per cent.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the commercial representative about the pool charge?”

title: The AGM question
scenario: Lot Owner: “Our budget's building management group recoveries line has jumped. Shared costs came to $131,600 against a $120,000 estimate, and our scheme's share is 45 per cent. I want it explained at the AGM in plain terms.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the increase?”

title: Approved
scenario: Contractor: “I'm chasing invoice 4471, $3,280 for gutter cleaning. Your system shows it as approved, but nothing has reached my account. I need confirmation today that it's been paid.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the contractor about the invoice?”

title: Right job, wrong code
scenario: Committee Member: “I'm the approver on a $1,640 Clearflow Plumbing invoice for a burst stairwell pipe. The work's done and the amount is right, but it's coded to garden maintenance instead of plumbing repairs. I plan to hold it until accounts fix the code.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the invoice?”

title: "Wrong code"
scenario: Accounts Payable Officer: “An approver wrote wrong code on a $480 invoice for pool deck lights. It's coded to pool chemicals. There's nothing else in the note, and I don't know which code they want.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the accounts payable officer about the note?”

title: "Seems high?"
scenario: Accounts Payable Officer: “An approver noted seems high on a $9,800 lift repair invoice and did nothing else. The quote was $8,200. The invoice is 20 days old and the contractor is ringing every day.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the accounts payable officer about the query?”

title: Mid-2024
scenario: Lot Owner: “I want the invoice for repainting the lobby by BrightCoat Painters, sometime in mid-2024. Your staff searched the invoice approval screen, which only shows this financial year, and told me nothing exists.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the missing invoice?”

title: 45 days overdue
scenario: Contractor: “Invoice 8812 for $2,140 is 45 days overdue and I want payment today. Apparently your ledger shows an EFT on 28 August, but nothing has hit my account. I changed banks in July.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the contractor about the payment?”

title: Wrong door
scenario: Team Member: “I was trying to recode a $600 cleaning invoice and ended up in journal entry JNL-3302. The code field is editable, so I'm going to fix it here.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the journal?”

title: Ten at once
scenario: Team Member: “A review found 10 invoices totalling $14,800 coded to the wrong accounts. I'm planning to spend this afternoon recoding them one by one.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the recoding?”

title: The claim
scenario: Accounts Officer: “A $5,600 Clearflow Plumbing invoice for a burst pipe that damaged three lots quotes insurance claim CLM-20419. It's coded to plumbing repairs and I'm about to approve it.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the accounts officer about the coding?”

title: Next to the red button
scenario: Team Member: “It's 11 am Tuesday and the payment run for 340 creditors is live. I need SparkRight's remittance now. The remittance screen sits right next to the reverse payment button.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about getting the remittance?”

title: Seeing double
scenario: Accounts Officer: “Clearflow Plumbing has sent invoices 5102 and 5102-A. Both are $1,640, dated the same day, with the same job description. The numbers are different, so I'm putting both in this week's run.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the accounts officer about the two invoices?”

title: GST twice
scenario: Committee Member: “SecureGate quoted $1,480 including GST to replace the pool gate closer. The invoice shows $1,480 plus $148 GST, $1,628 in total. I've been asked to approve it.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the invoice?”

title: Money we don't have?
scenario: Committee Member: “I'm new. The 30 September balance sheet shows contributions billed not due of $77,775. The notices went out on 1 September and are due 15 October. We haven't received that money, so I think the balance sheet is wrong.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the balance sheet?”

title: Good money, a liability
scenario: Committee Member: “The balance sheet shows contributions in advance of $9,400 as a liability. Eleven owners paid next quarter early. That money's in our bank, so how can it be a liability?”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the liability?”

title: The $400,000 bill
scenario: Treasurer: “We have $316,000 in the bank. The $400,000 building insurance premium is due 30 November. Other committed payments before then total $18,000, and we expect about $22,000 in arrears to come in. The next levy is due 1 January. I'm confident we'll manage.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about paying the premium?”

title: The missing money
scenario: Treasurer: “Our admin and sinking funds total $401,275 but the bank holds only $284,500. The balance sheet also shows arrears of $21,300, billed not due $77,775, prepaid insurance $46,000, creditors $18,900 and contributions in advance $9,400. I think money is missing.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the fund balances?”

title: 202 per cent
scenario: Treasurer: “Our electricity budget is $12,000 and we've spent $24,240, shown as 202 per cent. That includes a $9,800 January payment for last year's October to December bill, then three quarterly bills of about $4,800. I want to tell the AGM our power use has doubled.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the electricity figures?”

title: Off budget
scenario: Lot Owner: “The sinking fund report shows $12,400 paid to RoofTech on 18 August for roof membrane repairs. This year's sinking fund budget has nothing for roof works. I want to know who authorised it.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the payment?”

title: Six hundred bucks
scenario: Committee Member: “Our cleaning budget is $48,000 and we've spent $48,600 because of a one-off clean after a June leak. Our total admin budget is $640,000. I want the cleaning overspend listed as a major item at the next meeting.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the variance?”

title: The AI briefing
scenario: Team Member: “I used an AI tool to draft the committee's financial briefing. It says levies will comfortably cover the insurance shortfall by December and all arrears will be collected. Insurance is due 30 November, the next levy 1 January, and $16,500 of the $38,500 arrears is with the solicitor. I'm sending it tonight.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the draft briefing?”

title: The better rate
scenario: Treasurer: “We hold $190,000 in the sinking fund and will invest $150,000 from 20 October. A $60,000 roof payment is due in May. A six-month deposit matures around 20 April, but I prefer twelve months for the better rate.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the term?”

title: The low point
scenario: Chairperson: “We have $185,000 today. Over 12 weeks: $9,500 contract payments in weeks 4, 8 and 12; a $48,000 painting payment in week 4; about $70,000 of levies in week 6; and $92,000 insurance in week 10. We want to lock $50,000 in a three-month term deposit today.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the term deposit?”

title: Decide or note
scenario: Chairperson: “The briefing lists cash of $284,500, lot 18 arrears of $3,840.55 with a referral proposed, an $88,000 insurance renewal in January, electricity at 120 per cent of budget while next year's budget is prepared, and creditors of $18,900. I want every item put to a vote.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the briefing?”

scenario: Treasurer: “We've put $150,000 in a six-month term deposit at 4.6 per cent a year, with interest at maturity. I've told the committee it'll earn $6,900.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the interest figure?”

title: Can't you just run it?
scenario: Lot Owner: “Our 18-lot scheme had only one owner nominate at the AGM, so we have no committee. Most of us are too busy. Can't the body corporate manager just run it from now on?”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about running the scheme without a committee?”

title: Same template?
scenario: Team Member: “Westgate Business Park has had no committee since its AGM on 1 September. It's the same situation as Sunset Cove, so I'm using the Sunset Cove Part 5 agreement template and sending it out tomorrow.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the template?”

title: Still unsigned
scenario: Lot Owner: “The EGM on 2 September approved engaging the body corporate manager under Part 5 and authorised me to sign the agreement. I got one reminder email on 16 September and haven't got round to it. It's now 5 October. Does it really matter if it waits?”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about signing the agreement?”

title: Can't wait
scenario: Lot Owner: “We're under Part 5 with no committee. The first quarterly inspection is 14 October. We have cracked pool deck tiles, a pool gate closer that doesn't self-close and an overdue fire equipment service. I'm happy for all of it to wait for the inspection.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about these issues?”

title: The quiet report
scenario: Team Member: “I've drafted our Part 5 report for July to September. It covers routine maintenance and the financials. It doesn't mention the pool gate inspection, the overdue fire service, the $1,480 gate closer job or last quarter's outstanding actions. It's ready to send.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the draft report?”

title: The losing quote
scenario: Team Member: “Under Part 5 we're issuing a VOC for the pool gate closer. SecureGate quoted $1,480 and GatePro $1,720 for the same scope. We recommend SecureGate, so I've left GatePro's quote out of the owner papers to keep it simple.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the papers?”

title: One pair of hands
scenario: Lot Owner: “Under our Part 5 arrangement, the same person at the management firm engages contractors and approves their invoices. There's no second approver. The firm says owners get VOC notices and quarterly reports, so that's enough.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the controls?”

title: Saved to the desktop
scenario: Team Member: “The signed Part 5 agreement came back from lot 3 on 7 October. I saved it to the scheme folder on my laptop and marked the task complete.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the team member about the filing?”

title: A volunteer
scenario: Lot Owner: “We're three months into Part 5 management. I've got more time now and I'd be happy to join a committee. A staff member told me the Part 5 arrangement has to run its course.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about forming a committee?”

title: The brother-in-law
scenario: Lot Owner: “Our Part 5 manager recommended a $9,000 painting quote. I've since found out the painting company is owned by his brother-in-law. That wasn't disclosed anywhere in the VOC papers.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the recommendation?”

title: Nothing due
scenario: Chairperson: “At our 20 October meeting I'm proposing to drop the inspections register from the standing agenda because nothing is due this quarter. The lift registration renewal falls due on 30 January and the backflow test in February.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the agenda item?”

title: In his inbox
scenario: Committee Member: “The register shows a lift inspection on 12 August and a pool barrier inspection on 3 September, but neither report is on file. The building manager says they're somewhere in his inbox.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the missing reports?”

title: No rush
scenario: Chairperson: “Our insurance valuation is dated 12 February 2022. Insurance renews on 31 March 2027. There's no rush, so we'll arrange a new valuation sometime before renewal.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the valuation timing?”

title: The valuation motion
scenario: Treasurer: “We have two valuation quotes: ValuePro at $1,650 and Asset Assess at $1,980, both including GST, same scope. The committee wants ValuePro. I've drafted the motion as: That the valuation be done.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about the motion?”

title: Felt too high
scenario: Secretary: “Our 10-year sinking fund forecast recommends a $92,000 budget. We're proposing $78,100 because the $160,000 repaint moved from 2027 to 2029 after a building report found the paint sound. My draft minute says the committee felt the forecast was too high.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the secretary about the minute?”
topic: Recording reasons for departing from the forecast

title: Nobody's tripped yet
scenario: Chairperson: “A safety report dated 25 September rates a lifted paver on the main entry path as high risk, to be fixed within 7 days. Nobody has tripped yet, so I've told the manager to just file it.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the safety report?”

title: BlazeGuard does it all
scenario: Committee Member: “Our fire contractor BlazeGuard services all our fire equipment, so we don't need to pay for a fire safety adviser. I want that line taken out of next year's budget.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the fire safety adviser?”
topic: Fire contractor versus fire safety adviser

title: Spot the urgent one
scenario: Committee Member: “As of 5 October our register shows: lift registration expired 30 August, renewal not done; pool safety certificate expiring 14 March, copy not on file; backflow test due February, already booked. What do we tackle first?”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the committee member about the register?”

title: The $1 million unit
scenario: Lot Owner: “Our 28-lot building is insured for $28 million on the latest valuation. I've told my bank my unit is worth $1 million. That's just the valuation divided by the lots.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the lot owner about the valuation?”

title: Agreed by email
scenario: Chairperson: “On 1 October all five committee members agreed by email to a $3,200 quote to paint the pool fence. No notice went to owners and nothing's been recorded. It's unanimous, so please book the painter.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about engaging the painter?”

title: Seven days
scenario: Secretary: “Our committee approved $18,000 of fence repairs by VOC. The result was emailed to owners on Tuesday 3 November. The contractor wants to start on Monday 9 November.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the secretary about when the decision can be acted on?”

title: 48 signatures
scenario: Secretary: “Our scheme has 120 lots. Within the opposition period, we received a notice opposing the committee's $26,000 landscaping decision, with 48 signatures. Two are joint owners of the same lot and one signatory sold their lot in September. Some owners say the decision is dead.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the secretary about the notice of opposition?”

title: Levies by VOC
scenario: Treasurer: “Our insurance premium has risen by $40,000. The AGM is on 24 November. The committee wants to raise administrative fund contributions by VOC now, so the higher amount applies from 1 January.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the treasurer about raising the contributions?”

title: Four thumbs up
scenario: Chairperson: “Our committee has a WhatsApp group the manager isn't in. I asked whether we should approve SecureGate's $4,800 gate repair quote, and four of five replied agree. That's a majority, so please issue the work order.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the work order?”

title: "The painting"
scenario: Secretary: “I've drafted a VOC motion that reads: That the committee approves the painting. Nothing's attached. It's for stairwell painting by BrightCoat at $14,600 including GST, from the sinking fund.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the secretary about the motion?”

title: The unfinancial voter
scenario: Secretary: “Three of our five committee members voted yes on a VOC to replace the pool gate closer. One of them, the owner of lot 4, owed $1,240 in contributions due 1 October and still unpaid when they voted. I've recorded it as passed.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the secretary about the result?”
topic: Eligibility to vote on a VOC

title: Nine-fifteen
scenario: Chairperson: “Owners received the result of our committee VOC, and the 7-day opposition period ended at the end of Tuesday 10 November. At 9.15 am Wednesday, a notice of opposition signed by owners of 70 per cent of lots arrived by email. Owners say the decision is cancelled.”
instructions: “What should the body corporate manager advise the chairperson about the late notice?”
